thread:
Aarav: heads up — gitops pipeline pushed a canary of cni-addon 1.32 to eu-west-1 gpu pool a few mins ago, i'm seeing scheduling errors for pods that require the gpu nodeSelector.
Tess: seeing the same, several pods in Pending with FailedScheduling. quick kubectl: ```kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending
ml-train-abc-0   Pending   0/1     ContainerCreating   0     3m```
Maya: deploy-bot shows canary started by pipeline #4821 at 1779361200. any recent helm value changes? :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy triggered: repo=infra/charts, chart=cni-addon@1.32, env=eu-west-1/gpu, run=4821
Julien: can you paste `kubectl describe` for one of the pending pods? suspect nodeSelector/taint mismatch after the addon changed node label key.
Aarav: `kubectl describe pod ml-train-abc-0 -n ml` shows `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector.` Also `kubectl get nodes --show-labels | grep gpu` shows nodes labeled `redwood.io/gpu=true` but the cni-addon chart started reading `node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true` somehow.
Tess: oh — our nodegroup TF module sets label `redwood.io/gpu=true` historically. did the chart change to a different label in the canary?
Maya: chart diff from 1.28 -> 1.32 included a `nodeSelectorKey` defaulting to `node.kubernetes.io/gpu`. gitops values.yaml for env didn't override it.
Julien: that explains it. helm canary applied new default without env override. quick remediation options: 1) patch chart values to set nodeSelectorKey back, 2) patch nodes to also have the new label, 3) rollback canary. which is least-risk?
Aarav: patching nodes is ugly (changes infra out-of-band). rollback canary simple and fast. I'm in favor of quick rollback and then follow-up fix in gitops repo.
oncall-sre: also note: cluster-autoscaler started spawning c5.xlarge as fallback (no GPU), causing CPU cost surge for queries hitting scale-up. we should avoid spinning non-gpu workers for gpu workloads. adding to postmortem.
Maya: initiating rollback now. deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for cni-addon to 1.31 by Maya @ 1779361283.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete for canary (1 instance) at 1779361305 — status: success
Tess: pods started scheduling again after rollback — a few restarted, looks healthy. running a small smoke test: ```kubectl run cuda-smoke -n ml --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.0-base --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1' --restart=Never```
Julien: good call to rollback. follow-ups: - update infra/charts values in gitops to explicitly set `nodeSelectorKey: "redwood.io/gpu"` for gpu env - open PR to terragrunt/eks-module to add a second label alias so nodes carry both keys for a rolling window, or at least document label contract - add a CI check to detect chart value defaults that change nodeSelector/taint APIs
Aarav: i'm creating the gitops PR now to pin the value + adding a canary checklist step to verify node labels before deploy.
Maya: also filing ticket INFRA-2783: "CNI chart default nodeSelector drift caused gpu scheduling failure" with timeline and cost note about autoscaler spawn. assign to eng-infra and cc sres.
oncall-sre: please add the terraform state check — I ran `terraform plan` against prod infra and noticed recent manual edit in `module.gpu_nodegroup.tags` that removed a managed tag. not the taint, but we should audit for drift: ```Warning: Resource has changed outside of Terraform```
Tess: for prevention: propose adding an automated pre-canary hook: `kubectl get nodes -l redwood.io/gpu=true --no-headers | wc -l` and fail canary if zero. i'll draft the job.
Julien: +1. Also let's add a smoke pod schedule test to the canary pipeline that requests a GPU and fails the canary if it can't schedule within 2 minutes.
Maya: agreed. tagging this thread with :white_check_mark: once PRs merged. thanks team, saved a potential wider outage and cost drift.
Aarav: thanks all — follow-up owners: Maya (gitops PR), Tess (canary hook), Julien (TF audit), oncall-sre (postmortem + cost calc).
Maya: will post links to PRs and the incident ticket in this thread shortly. :rocket:
